name: Subterranean Sandwich Authority
address: 1 Federal Sandwich Plaza, Sublevel 3, Suite B-0, Grandview Commons Office Park, Exit 41B
about: The Subterranean Sandwich Authority is a federally chartered agency responsible for the intake, review, and issuance of sandwiches within this jurisdiction. Submitting an application does not guarantee a sandwich. Determinations are final and are not disclosed.
announcement: The $5 Footlong promotion concluded in 2016. Signage removal is scheduled and funded. Pricing is unaffected.

reviews.name: Denise R.
reviews.text: My application was denied at the counter and I was billed for the denial. The sandwich I eventually received was excellent.

reviews.name: Marcus H.
reviews.text: Waited fifty-one minutes in the rope maze. The take-a-number dispenser was fully stocked, which I appreciated.

reviews.name: P. Vandergriff
reviews.text: Closes at 4:30 PM. I work until 5. I have not eaten here in four years and I continue to order.

reviews.name: Tonya B.
reviews.text: I declined the bun and was charged for the bun. Staff explained the bake had already occurred. That is fair.

reviews.name: Gerald Okonkwo
reviews.text: The meatball determination came back favorable. Sauce reached my mailbox before I did.

menu.name: Form 6-B: Footlong Determinations
menu.blurb: Twelve inches as defined by federal standard. Standard subject to revision without notice.

items.name: The Federally Measured Footlong
items.desc: A submarine sandwich measured against the Authority's reference rail. If it measures short, the rail is recalibrated and the sandwich is issued.
items.imagePrompt: Ultra-premium commercial food photography for a delivery-app menu tile. Subject: one enormous twelve-inch cold-cut submarine sandwich laid dead straight on a stainless steel prep rail, the lid of bread lifted and propped so shingled folds of pale deli meat spill over both long edges and sag onto the metal, shredded lettuce avalanching out, oil pooling in a bright slick under the loaf. Setting: a laminated stainless prep rail behind a scratched acrylic sneeze guard, institutional beige tile wall, a blank unmarked laminated form taped to the glass. Lighting: flat cold overhead fluorescent tube light, no shadow drama, bureaucratic and slightly green, unflattering and honest. Camera: strict overhead flat-lay, 50mm, deep focus edge to edge, flat clinical contrast, every crumb visible. Square crop, subject centered and filling the frame. Deadpan hyperreal advertising realism. No text, no logos, no packaging labels, no hands, no people.

items.desc: Three classifications of pressed deli meat, folded into a roll by an employee holding a clipboard. Tier assignment is final.
items.imagePrompt: A careless snapshot taken on an old cheap smartphone by a restaurant employee to upload to a food delivery app. Subject: a twelve-inch roll folded shut over three shingled layers of pressed deli meat — ham, salami and bologna — with shredded lettuce and two tomato discs pushing out along the seam, laid in a white styrofoam clamshell with the lid propped back. Flat overhead fluorescent tube light with a green-yellow cast, no fill and mixed white balance. Framed slightly crooked with the clamshell cut off at the right edge on a stainless prep counter, a napkin dispenser and a stack of plastic lids behind it. Flat, unretouched phone-camera look.. EVERYTHING in the frame equally sharp from the food to the back wall - no shallow depth of field, no bokeh, no blurred background, no food styling. Aggressive default smartphone HDR processing: over-sharpened with visible halos along every edge, shadows lifted grey and blotchy, mushy chroma noise, heavy JPEG compression, slightly wrong white balance. The container is off-centre and clipped by one edge of the frame, the camera tilted several degrees off level, shot from too close and slightly above. This is a careless snapshot, NOT a photograph: no artistic composition, no cinematic lighting, no colour grading, no professional food photography, nothing centred or plated. Unstyled, unretouched, honest and a little unappetising - but the food is real food from a real kitchen, generous and identifiable, not a joke about bad food. Square crop. items.imagePrompt: A careless snapshot taken on an old cheap smartphone by a restaurant employee to upload to a food delivery app. Subject: one large double chocolate cookie, dark and cracked across the top with chunks of chocolate showing through and a soft sag in the middle, sitting on a square of wax paper on a white paper plate. Dim warm restaurant light with the flash off, slightly underexposed and noisy, unretouched. Framed slightly crooked with the plate cut off at the left edge, another order waiting on the prep counter behind.. EVERYTHING in the frame equally sharp from the food to the back wall - no shallow depth of field, no bokeh, no blurred background, no food styling. Aggressive default smartphone HDR processing: over-sharpened with visible halos along every edge, shadows lifted grey and blotchy, mushy chroma noise, heavy JPEG compression, slightly wrong white balance. The container is off-centre and clipped by one edge of the frame, the camera tilted several degrees off level, shot from too close and slightly above. This is a careless snapshot, NOT a photograph: no artistic composition, no cinematic lighting, no colour grading, no professional food photography, nothing centred or plated. Unstyled, unretouched, honest and a little unappetising - but the food is real food from a real kitchen, generous and identifiable, not a joke about bad food. Square crop. No text, no letters, no words, no numbers, no writing or printing on any container, cup, wrapper, bag or sign, no logos, no labels, no watermarks, no people, no hands.
